factProposals.value: Reads Basecamp 3/4 project data read-only from https://3.basecampapi.com/{account_id}: the project dock, the message board's messages (one message = one submission) and each message's comments, following Link-header pagination.

Basecamp offers no API keys; the only access is an OAuth 2.0 bearer token from 37signals Launchpad, which requires a registered app (client id/secret) and one browser authorization by a Basecamp user. The app then sees exactly what that user can see.

Attachments and links are not separate API fields: they are embedded in message and comment HTML as <bc-attachment> tags and <a href> links. @mentions use the same <bc-attachment> tag and must be excluded.

SQL Server's Basecamp_MessageBoards_MessageComments CommentId and MessageId values (about 1.0e9 to 1.03e10) are Basecamp recording ids, the same ids the Basecamp API returns, so a comment from either source maps to the same Review Queue item.

Every retrieval writes submission_retrieval_started and then _completed or _failed JSON log lines carrying a timestamp, the requesting user id, the project id, a correlation id, counts and an error class.
Who registers the Basecamp OAuth app and whose Basecamp account authorizes it (personal login vs. a company/service account) is not yet decided.

decisions.statement: A submission is a message on the project's message board, together with its comments.
decisions.rationale: Matches the SQL data, where each Stress Test step points to a message board message; confirmed with the student.

decisions.statement: Use httpx as the runtime HTTP client for Basecamp.
decisions.rationale: Already pinned for tests; its MockTransport lets every failure path be tested without a network. User-approved dependency change.

decisions.statement: Build and verify against a simulated Basecamp API now; connect live once an OAuth app is registered.
decisions.rationale: The student cannot provide a client id/secret today, and a username/password shortcut would break REQ-012 and the no-credentials guardrail.

decisions.statement: Never retry 401/403; retry 429 after Retry-After (capped at 30 s) and 5xx/network errors, at most 3 attempts; never follow redirects or non-https pagination links.
decisions.rationale: A rejected token fails the same way again, and the bearer token must never be sent to another host or in clear text.

limitations.statement: Not yet run against live Basecamp: no OAuth app is registered, so all verification uses simulated API responses.
The access token expires after about two weeks and is not refreshed automatically during retrieval; re-running the setup script gets a new one.
Retrieval runs from a command-line script; the audit user id is supplied by the caller because the app has no user authentication yet.
Attachment files are listed (name, type, URL) but not downloaded.
Only the message board is read; files uploaded to a project's Docs & Files are not retrieved.
